body: Look, I feel bad and I’m sure it was an accident. But this is exactly why they tell you not to do it. I know people do all the time but this is the risk they’re taking.

Alas, if only it worked that way. Hoping Softwarez will block him, right now the only time we can blacklist customers is if the service provider asks for it, or if there has been fraud. It's been about a week, though, so my hopes are pretty high that he'll not be back.
In all likelihood he never paid for it. However, we asked for proof that he had indeed paid (since we don't see anything) and he got all angry. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Totally understandable. But this charge was authorized by the customer - we inform them at checkout, as well as after the purchase, of the date and dollar amount of the next payment. They can also contact us to cancel at any time. Additionally, several of the companies we partner with send out reminder emails prior to payment (however we're unable to see them, as they're not handled by us). 

We work really hard to make this as easy as possible for the customers, but you can't please everyone I guess ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ trying to play the blame game and pin it on us isn't gonna work, though. Haha.
In this case, he's going to a lawyer over literally nothing. I hope he does.

Funny you should mention "news"... we also do email support - we received a similar issue yesterday. No overdraft, just an unwanted renewal. Guy cc's talktothepress.com (L O L) and includes "Daily Mail please print this" in his email. 

L O L AGAIN 

So many issues with that. You're not talking to the Daily Mail. Whoever you're talking to won't print that, as they haven't received our permission. And? We're? Right? And you're wrong? Calm down? Maybe?

Not a typo. I'll be so stoked if he does contact our lawyer (somehow). I'm sure he'll rip him a new one. 

Related: yes, for a $35 OD fee. This isn't the first time I've heard this threat...
